topics.label: Lecture Introduction: Initiation and Resolution of Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecture by framing the session as a deeper exploration into the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Principles of Innate Immune Recognition
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the fundamental concepts of innate immune sensing, including how molecular patterns of pathogens and tissue damage are defined, distinguished from self, and targeted by cellular receptors.

topics.label: Pattern Recognition Receptor Families and Signaling
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the major classes of pattern recognition receptors, their subcellular signaling pathways, and the assembly of inflammasome complexes to activate inflammatory cytokines.

topics.label: Leukocyte Recruitment, Trafficking, and Systemic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace the cellular mechanisms and physiological consequences of leukocyte activation, tissue extravasation, and lymphatic trafficking during an inflammatory response.

topics.label: Resolution of Inflammation, Tissue Repair, and Chronic Inflammation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the mechanisms that terminate acute inflammation and govern subsequent tissue outcomes, ranging from healing to chronic inflammatory states.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the complement system.
